title: Guayaquil Junta
capsule: The Guayaquil Junta was a short-lived autonomous governing body established in the port city of Guayaquil during the complex independence struggles along the Pacific coast of South America, operating between 1812 and 1814 while Quito remained under royalist control following the suppression of the Quito autonomy junta in 1812. The junta reflected Guayaquil's distinct commercial identity as a port city and represented an early, tentative assertion of local self-governance within the broader context of the Ecuadorian wars of independence. It was re-absorbed into the Spanish colonial system before the decisive Guayaquil independence proclamation of October 9, 1820 that led to the port's eventual incorporation into Gran Colombia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. This entity is poorly attested in English-language scholarship; the 1812–1814 Guayaquil Junta appears to be a minor local administrative body and its geographic extent and precise chronology are uncertain.
